+# Python Port Architecture
+
+## Compatibility contract
+
+The evaluator invokes the rebuilt command with the same arguments, working
+directory, environment, stdin, and filesystem as eza v0.23.3. Compatibility is
+defined by the exact process exit status and raw stdout and stderr bytes. The
+benchmark scope is directory listing, long view, tree traversal, sorting, and
+hidden-file handling with icons and colours disabled.
+
+## Design
+
+`eza_port.py` is a standalone standard-library Python program. It is split into
+four behavioral layers that mirror stable boundaries in the Rust source:
+
+1. A hand-written option parser preserves eza's long options, clustered short
+   options, attached values, `--` handling, rightmost-option precedence, and
+   option errors.
+2. Filesystem records cache lstat-style metadata and expose eza concepts such
+   as file kind, Windows attributes, symlink target, size, and timestamps.
+3. Filtering and ordering apply hidden-file rules, ignore globs, type filters,
+   natural sorting, reversal, and directory grouping before rendering.
+4. Renderers implement line, grid, long-table, recursive, and tree output while
+   writing UTF-8 with LF line endings directly to binary stdout/stderr.
+
+The implementation never invokes the reference binary and has no third-party
+runtime dependency. The official binary is used only by the test harness.
+
+## Entrypoints
+
+`compile.sh` performs a Python syntax check and creates exactly one
+platform-appropriate highest-priority evaluator entrypoint. On Windows this is
+`executable.cmd`; on Unix it is the Python source `executable` with a shebang.
+The script removes stale evaluator entrypoints and is idempotent.
+
+## Backward-compatibility verification
+
+`.tura/script/differential_test.py` builds deterministic temporary directory
+fixtures and runs a manifest of representative invocations against both the
+official executable from `REFERENCE_BINARY.txt` and the rebuilt entrypoint. It
+compares status, stdout bytes, and stderr bytes independently and emits a
+focused mismatch report. Static syntax/build checks and focused smoke tests run
+before the full differential manifest.
+
+## Deliberate scope boundaries
+
+Colour themes, icons, Git integration, extended attributes, and terminal-only
+presentation are outside the stated benchmark behavior. Their options are
+parsed where needed for compatible disabled-mode behavior, but the core port
+does not duplicate those optional subsystems. This boundary must not weaken any
+listing, metadata, traversal, filtering, ordering, process-I/O, or error behavior
+inside the benchmark scope.
*** End Patch

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Byte-for-byte compatibility tests for the local eza Python port."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+
+
+def reference_binary() -> Path:
+    return Path((ROOT / "REFERENCE_BINARY.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
+
+
+def rebuilt_command() -> list[str]:
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        return [os.environ.get("COMSPEC", "cmd.exe"), "/d", "/c", str(ROOT / "executable.cmd")]
+    return [str(ROOT / "executable")]
+
+
+def make_fixture(root: Path) -> None:
+    (root / "alpha").mkdir()
+    (root / "alpha" / "nested").mkdir()
+    (root / "empty-dir").mkdir()
+    (root / ".dotdir").mkdir()
+    (root / "_private").mkdir()
+    files = {
+        ".hidden": b"hidden",
+        "_under": b"under",
+        "A2.txt": b"a",
+        "a10.TXT": b"abcdefghij",
+        "plain": b"plain",
+        "has space.md": b"space",
+        "has'quote": b"quote",
+        "alpha/child2": b"22",
+        "alpha/child10": b"1010101010",
+        "alpha/nested/leaf.log": b"leaf",
+    }
+    for name, data in files.items():
+        (root / name).write_bytes(data)
+
+
+def cases(fixture: Path) -> list[tuple[str, list[str], bytes, dict[str, str]]]:
+    path = str(fixture)
+    child = str(fixture / "plain")
+    missing = str(fixture / "missing")
+    base = ["--color=never", "--icons=never"]
+    return [
+        ("lines", base + ["--oneline", path], b"", {}),
+        ("almost-all", base + ["--oneline", "--almost-all", path], b"", {}),
+        ("all-twice", base + ["--oneline", "-aa", path], b"", {}),
+        ("name-case", base + ["--oneline", "--sort=Name", path], b"", {}),
+        ("extension", base + ["--oneline", "--sort=extension", path], b"", {}),
+        ("size-reverse", base + ["--oneline", "--sort=size", "--reverse", path], b"", {}),
+        ("type-dirs-first", base + ["--oneline", "--sort=type", "--group-directories-first", path], b"", {}),
+        ("ignore", base + ["--oneline", "--ignore-glob=*.txt|plain", path], b"", {}),
+        ("only-dirs", base + ["--oneline", "--only-dirs", path], b"", {}),
+        ("explicit", base + ["--oneline", child], b"", {}),
+        ("missing-and-file", base + ["--oneline", missing, child], b"", {}),
+        ("long-stable", base + ["--long", "--no-user", "--no-time", path], b"", {}),
+        ("long-header", base + ["--long", "--header", "--no-user", "--no-time", "--bytes", path], b"", {}),
+        ("tree", base + ["--tree", path], b"", {}),
+        ("tree-level", base + ["--tree", "--level=2", path], b"", {}),
+        ("recursive", base + ["--recurse", "--level=2", "--oneline", path], b"", {}),
+        ("classify", base + ["--oneline", "--classify=always", path], b"", {}),
+        ("grid", base + ["--grid", "--width=32", path], b"", {}),
+        ("grid-across", base + ["--grid", "--across", "--width=32", path], b"", {}),
+        ("stdin", base + ["--oneline", "--stdin"], (child + "\n").encode(), {}),
+        ("unknown-option", ["--not-an-eza-option"], b"", {}),
+        ("bad-sort", ["--sort=invalid"], b"", {}),
+        ("version", ["--version"], b"", {}),
+        ("help", ["--help"], b"", {}),
+    ]
+
+
+def invoke(command: list[str], argv: list[str], stdin: bytes, env_updates: dict[str, str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env.update(env_updates)
+    return subprocess.run(
+        command + argv,
+        cwd=ROOT,
+        env=env,
+        input=stdin,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def preview(data: bytes) -> str:
+    text = data.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace")
+    return repr(text[:500] + ("..." if len(text) > 500 else ""))
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", default=[], help="run only the named case")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    reference = reference_binary()
+    if not reference.is_file():
+        parser.error(f"reference binary does not exist: {reference}")
+
+    temp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="eza-port-diff-"))
+    failures = 0
+    try:
+        fixture = temp / "fixture"
+        fixture.mkdir()
+        make_fixture(fixture)
+        selected = [case for case in cases(fixture) if not args.case or case[0] in args.case]
+        for name, argv, stdin, env in selected:
+            expected = invoke([str(reference)], argv, stdin, env)
+            actual = invoke(rebuilt_command(), argv, stdin, env)
+            differences = []
+            if expected.returncode != actual.returncode:
+                differences.append(f"status {expected.returncode} != {actual.returncode}")
+            if expected.stdout != actual.stdout:
+                differences.append(f"stdout\n  ref={preview(expected.stdout)}\n  got={preview(actual.stdout)}")
+            if expected.stderr != actual.stderr:
+                differences.append(f"stderr\n  ref={preview(expected.stderr)}\n  got={preview(actual.stderr)}")
+            if differences:
+                failures += 1
+                print(f"FAIL {name}: " + "\n".join(differences))
+            else:
+                print(f"PASS {name}")
+    finally:
+        shutil.rmtree(temp, ignore_errors=True)
+
+    print(f"{len(selected) - failures}/{len(selected)} differential cases passed")
+    return 1 if failures else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
*** End Patch

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""A benchmark-focused Python port of eza 0.23.3.

+the pinned Rust source. It intentionally uses only the Python standard library.
+"""
+

+

+

+

+

+  --no-permissions           suppress the permissions field
+  --no-filesize              suppress the filesize field
+  --no-user                  suppress the user field
+  --no-time                  suppress the time field
+  --stdin                    read file names from stdin, one per line or other separator

+  --git                      list each file's Git status, if tracked or ignored
+  --no-git                   suppress Git status (always overrides --git,

+  --git-repos                list root of git-tree status

+
+WHEN = ("always", "auto", "never")
+SORT_CHOICES = (
+    "name", "Name", "size", "extension", "Extension", "modified",
+    "changed", "accessed", "created", "inode", "type", "none",

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ArgSpec:
+    short: str | None
+    long: str
+    value_kind: str = "forbidden"
+    choices: tuple[str, ...] | None = None
+    default: str | None = None
+
+    def option_name(self) -> str:
+        suffix = f" (-{self.short})" if self.short is not None else ""
+        return f"--{self.long}{suffix}"
+
+
+def spec(short: str | None, long: str, kind: str = "forbidden",
+         choices: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, default: str | None = None) -> ArgSpec:
+    return ArgSpec(short, long, kind, choices, default)
+
+
+SPECS = [
+    spec("v", "version"), spec("?", "help"),
+    spec("1", "oneline"), spec("l", "long"), spec("G", "grid"),
+    spec("x", "across"), spec("R", "recurse"), spec("T", "tree"),
+    spec("F", "classify", "optional", WHEN, "auto"),
+    spec("X", "dereference"), spec("w", "width", "necessary"),
+    spec(None, "no-quotes"),
+    spec(None, "absolute", "optional", ("on", "follow", "off"), "on"),
+    spec(None, "follow-symlinks"),
+    spec(None, "color", "optional", WHEN, "auto"),
+    spec(None, "colour", "optional", WHEN, "auto"),
+    spec(None, "color-scale", "optional", ("all", "size", "age"), "all"),
+    spec(None, "colour-scale", "optional", ("all", "size", "age"), "all"),
+    spec(None, "color-scale-mode", "necessary", ("fixed", "gradient")),
+    spec(None, "colour-scale-mode", "necessary", ("fixed", "gradient")),
+    spec("a", "all"), spec("A", "almost-all"),
+    spec("d", "treat-dirs-as-files"), spec(None, "list-dirs"),
+    spec("L", "level", "necessary"), spec("r", "reverse"),
+    spec("s", "sort", "necessary", SORT_CHOICES),
+    spec("I", "ignore-glob", "necessary"), spec(None, "git-ignore"),
+    spec(None, "group-directories-first"), spec(None, "group-directories-last"),
+    spec("D", "only-dirs"), spec("f", "only-files"),
+    spec(None, "no-symlinks"), spec(None, "show-symlinks"),
+    spec("b", "binary"), spec("B", "bytes"), spec("g", "group"),
+    spec("n", "numeric"), spec("h", "header"),
+    spec(None, "icons", "optional", WHEN, "auto"),
+    spec("i", "inode"), spec("H", "links"), spec("m", "modified"),
+    spec(None, "changed"), spec("S", "blocksize"), spec(None, "total-size"),
+    spec("t", "time", "necessary", TIME_CHOICES), spec("u", "accessed"),
+    spec("U", "created"), spec(None, "time-style", "necessary", TIME_STYLE_CHOICES),
+    spec(None, "hyperlink"), spec("M", "mounts"), spec(None, "smart-group"),
+    spec(None, "no-permissions"), spec(None, "no-filesize"),
+    spec(None, "no-user"), spec(None, "no-time"),
+    spec(None, "git"), spec(None, "no-git"), spec(None, "git-repos"),
+    spec(None, "git-repos-no-status"), spec("@", "extended"),
+    spec("o", "octal-permissions"), spec("Z", "context"),
+    spec(None, "stdin"), spec("O", "flags"),
+]
+BY_LONG = {item.long: item for item in SPECS}
+BY_SHORT = {item.short: item for item in SPECS if item.short is not None}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Flag:
+    kind: str
+    text: str
+
+    def __str__(self) -> str:
+        return ("--" if self.kind == "long" else "-") + self.text
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Match:
+    spec: ArgSpec
+    flag: Flag
+    value: str | None
+
+
+class OptionFailure(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def choices_text(values: Sequence[str]) -> str:
+    return "choices: " + ", ".join(values)
+
+
+def debug_string(value: str) -> str:
+    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
+
+
+class MatchedFlags:
+    def __init__(self, matches: list[Match], strict: bool):
+        self.matches = matches
+        self.strict = strict
+
+    def records(self, *names: str, with_value: bool | None = None) -> list[Match]:
+        result = [item for item in self.matches if item.spec.long in names]
+        if with_value is not None:
+            result = [item for item in result if (item.value is not None) == with_value]
+        return result
+
+    def count(self, name: str) -> int:
+        return len(self.records(name))
+
+    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        found = self.records(name, with_value=False)
+        if self.strict and len(found) > 1:
+            self._duplicate(found)
+        return bool(found)
+
+    def has_any(self, names: Sequence[str]) -> Match | None:
+        found = [item for item in self.matches if item.spec.long in names and item.value is None]
+        if self.strict and len(found) > 1:
+            self._duplicate(found)
+        return found[-1] if found else None
+
+    def get(self, name: str) -> str | None:
+        found = self.records(name, with_value=True)
+        if self.strict and len(found) > 1:
+            self._duplicate(found)
+        return found[-1].value if found else None
+
+    def get_any(self, names: Sequence[str]) -> Match | None:
+        found = [item for item in self.matches if item.spec.long in names and item.value is not None]
+        if self.strict and len(found) > 1:
+            self._duplicate(found)
+        return found[-1] if found else None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _duplicate(found: Sequence[Match]) -> None:
+        a, b = found[0].flag, found[1].flag
+        if a == b:
+            raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {a} was given twice")
+        raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {a} conflicts with flag {b}")
+
+
+def parse_arguments(argv: Sequence[str], strict: bool) -> tuple[MatchedFlags, list[str]]:
+    matches: list[Match] = []
+    frees: list[str] = []
+    parsing = True
+    index = 0
+    while index < len(argv):
+        token = argv[index]
+        index += 1
+        if not parsing:
+            frees.append(token)
+            continue
+        if token == "--":
+            parsing = False
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            raw = token[2:]
+            before, separator, after = raw.partition("=")
+            split = bool(separator and before and after)
+            name = before if split else raw
+            item = BY_LONG.get(name)
+            if item is None:
+                raise OptionFailure(f"Unknown argument --{name}")
+            flag = Flag("long", item.long)
+            if split:
+                if item.value_kind == "forbidden":
+                    raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {flag} cannot take a value")
+                matches.append(Match(item, flag, after))
+            elif item.value_kind == "forbidden":
+                matches.append(Match(item, flag, None))
+            elif item.value_kind == "necessary":
+                if index >= len(argv):
+                    suffix = f" ({choices_text(item.choices)})" if item.choices else ""
+                    raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {flag} needs a value{suffix}")
+                matches.append(Match(item, flag, argv[index]))
+                index += 1
+            else:
+                value = item.default
+                if index < len(argv) and item.choices and argv[index] in item.choices:
+                    value = argv[index]
+                    index += 1
+                matches.append(Match(item, flag, value))
+            continue
+        if token.startswith("-") and token != "-":
+            raw = token[1:]
+            before, separator, after = raw.partition("=")
+            if separator and before and after:
+                ordinary = before[:-1]
+                valued = before[-1]
+                for char in ordinary:
+                    item = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                    if item is None:
+                        raise OptionFailure(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                    flag = Flag("short", char)
+                    if item.value_kind == "necessary":
+                        suffix = f" ({choices_text(item.choices)})" if item.choices else ""
+                        raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {flag} needs a value{suffix}")
+                    value = item.default if item.value_kind == "optional" else None
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, value))
+                item = BY_SHORT.get(valued)
+                if item is None:
+                    raise OptionFailure(f"Unknown argument -{valued}")
+                flag = Flag("short", valued)
+                if item.value_kind == "forbidden":
+                    raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {flag} cannot take a value")
+                matches.append(Match(item, flag, after))
+                continue
+            position = 0
+            while position < len(raw):
+                char = raw[position]
+                position += 1
+                item = BY_SHORT.get(char)
+                if item is None:
+                    raise OptionFailure(f"Unknown argument -{char}")
+                flag = Flag("short", char)
+                tail = raw[position:]
+                if item.value_kind == "forbidden":
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, None))
+                    continue
+                if item.value_kind == "necessary":
+                    if tail:
+                        matches.append(Match(item, flag, tail))
+                    elif index < len(argv):
+                        matches.append(Match(item, flag, argv[index]))
+                        index += 1
+                    else:
+                        suffix = f" ({choices_text(item.choices)})" if item.choices else ""
+                        raise OptionFailure(f"Flag {flag} needs a value{suffix}")
+                    break
+                if tail and item.choices and tail in item.choices:
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, tail))
+                    break
+                if tail.startswith("="):
+                    value = tail[1:]
+                    if not value:
+                        raise OptionFailure(f"Unknown argument -=")
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, value))
+                    break
+                if not tail and index < len(argv) and item.choices and argv[index] in item.choices:
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, argv[index]))
+                    index += 1
+                else:
+                    matches.append(Match(item, flag, item.default))
+            continue
+        frees.append(token)
+    return MatchedFlags(matches, strict), frees
+
+
+def bad_argument(item: ArgSpec, value: str) -> OptionFailure:
+    suffix = f" ({choices_text(item.choices)})" if item.choices else ""
+    return OptionFailure(
+        f"Option {item.option_name()} has no {debug_string(value)} setting{suffix}"
+    )
+
+
+def parse_usize(value: str, item: ArgSpec) -> int:
+    if not value or not value.isdecimal():
+        detail = "invalid digit found in string"
+        raise OptionFailure(
+            f"Value {debug_string(value)} not valid for option {item.option_name()}: {detail}"
+        )
+    return int(value)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Options:
+    mode: str = "lines"
+    width: int | None = None
+    is_tty: bool = False
+    across: bool = False
+    dir_action: str = "list"
+    level: int | None = None
+    dot_filter: str = "just"
+    sort: str = "name"
+    reverse: bool = False
+    dirs_first: bool = False
+    dirs_last: bool = False
+    ignore_patterns: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    only_dirs: bool = False
+    only_files: bool = False
+    no_symlinks: bool = False
+    show_symlinks: bool = False
+    quote: bool = True
+    classify: str = "never"
+    absolute: str = "off"
+    dereference: bool = False
+    follow_symlinks: bool = False
+    stdin: bool = False
+    header: bool = False
+    permissions: bool = True
+    filesize: bool = True
+    user: bool = True
+    size_format: str = "decimal"
+    time_style: str = "default"
+    time_types: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["modified"])
+    file_flags: bool = False
+    links: bool = False
+    inode: bool = False
+    group: bool = False
+    blocksize: bool = False
+    octal: bool = False
+    numeric: bool = False
+    total_size: bool = False
+
+
+def deduce_options(flags: MatchedFlags, environ: dict[str, str]) -> Options:
+    result = Options()
+
+    width_value = flags.get("width")
+    if width_value is not None:
+        parsed = parse_usize(width_value, BY_LONG["width"])
+        result.width = parsed if parsed >= 1 else None
+        result.is_tty = parsed >= 1
+    elif "COLUMNS" in environ:
+        value = environ["COLUMNS"]
+        if not value.isdecimal():
+            raise OptionFailure(
+                f"Value {debug_string(value)} not valid for environment variable COLUMNS: invalid digit found in string"
+            )
+        result.width = int(value)
+        result.is_tty = True
+    else:
+        result.is_tty = sys.stdout.isatty()
+        if result.is_tty:
+            result.width = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24)).columns
+
+    primary = flags.has_any(("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree"))
+    if primary is None:
+        result.mode = "grid" if result.is_tty else "lines"
+    elif primary.spec.long == "long" or (
+        primary.spec.long in ("tree", "grid") and flags.has("long")
+    ):
+        grid_or_tree = flags.has_any(("grid", "tree"))
+        result.mode = "grid-details" if grid_or_tree and grid_or_tree.spec.long == "grid" else "details"
+    elif primary.spec.long == "tree":
+        result.mode = "tree"
+    elif primary.spec.long == "oneline":
+        result.mode = "lines"
+    else:
+        result.mode = "grid"
+
+    result.across = flags.has("across")
+    recurse = flags.has("recurse")
+    as_file = flags.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or flags.has("list-dirs")
+    tree = flags.has("tree")
+    can_tree = result.mode in ("tree", "details")
+    if tree and can_tree:
+        result.dir_action = "tree"
+    elif recurse:

You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

input.fullContext:
You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Run the applicable original trycmd snapshots against the rebuilt command."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+REFERENCE_ROOT = ROOT / "rust-reference"
+
+
+def executable_command() -> list[str]:
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        return [str(ROOT / "executable.cmd")]
+    return [str(ROOT / "executable")]
+
+
+def snapshot(name: str) -> bytes:
+    return (REFERENCE_ROOT / "tests" / "cmd" / f"{name}.stdout").read_bytes().replace(
+        b"\r\n", b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    expected_absolute = (
+        str((REFERENCE_ROOT / "tests" / "itest" / "index.svg").resolve()) + "\n"
+    ).encode("utf-8")
+    cases = [
+        ("basic_all", ["tests/itest"], snapshot("basic_all")),
+        (
+            "absolute_file_all",
+            ["tests/itest/index.svg", "--absolute"],
+            expected_absolute,
+        ),
+    ]
+    if os.name == "nt":
+        cases.append((
+            "long_windows",
+            [
+                "tests/itest", "--long", "--no-user", "--no-time",
+                "--no-filesize",
+            ],
+            snapshot("long_windows"),
+        ))
+
+    command = executable_command()
+    if not Path(command[0]).is_file():
+        print(f"missing rebuilt entrypoint: {command[0]}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    environment = os.environ.copy()
+    for name in (
+        "COLUMNS", "EZA_CONFIG_DIR", "EZA_GRID_ROWS", "EXA_GRID_ROWS",
+        "EZA_STDIN_SEPARATOR", "EZA_STRICT", "EXA_STRICT", "TIME_STYLE",
+    ):
+        environment.pop(name, None)
+
+    failures = 0
+    for name, argv, expected_stdout in cases:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            command + argv,
+            cwd=REFERENCE_ROOT,
+            env=environment,
+            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+            check=False,
+        )
+        differences = []
+        if result.returncode != 0:
+            differences.append(f"status={result.returncode}")
+        if result.stdout != expected_stdout:
+            differences.append("stdout differs")
+        if result.stderr:
+            differences.append(f"stderr={result.stderr!r}")
+        if differences:
+            failures += 1
+            print(f"FAIL {name}: {', '.join(differences)}")
+        else:
+            print(f"PASS {name}")
+
+    print(f"{len(cases) - failures}/{len(cases)} original snapshots passed")
+    return 1 if failures else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
*** End Patch
